free_tier.stated: No free tier; a paid usenet account.
free_tier.notes: No price is quoted because the pricing page was not read.

per_object_cap.stated: Not published; the unit is the article.

retention.stated: 'UsenetServer offers one of the highest article retention times available'; no day count on the page read.

egress.terms: Unmetered on an unlimited plan; article availability binds before bytes.

record.interface_detail: NNTP reader, TLS; standard article commands.
record.chaining: The clearest documented split between the two article codes: 423 means the group is there and the article is not, 430 means the article is unavailable while the group remains readable, which is what a script can branch on.

limits.value: articles past retention answer 423 or 430 per article id
plan connection count is the ceiling; excess connections are refused at connect time
50 SSL connections on the 12-month plan, 20 on the 1-month

record.limits_note: The vendor points at indexers as the amplifier: 'Many Indexers maintain references to articles long after they've been removed from Usenet servers', so the NZB can be valid and the articles still gone.
record.binding_note: Unlimited bytes; the first failure is a per-article 430/423 whose frequency is set by the indexer's freshness and the spool's retention.

identity_cost.detail: Paid account with email and card. No identity document described.

record.reliability_note: An indexer can point at articles the spool no longer holds; each such article is a per-file failure and only PAR2 or a second provider recovers it.
record.confidence_note: The 423/430 distinction and the indexer behaviour are the vendor's own. No removal-by-notice cause is named on this page, which differs from Newshosting's page in the same group.

evidence.proved: '423 No Such Article: The server acknowledges the group exists, but the article requested is not present. 430 No Such Article: The article is not available on the server, even though the newsgroup is accessible.' And 'Many Indexers maintain references to articles long after they've been removed from Usenet servers.'
Second server behaviour: a backup account is only asked after every primary has answered no such article; a second server turns a whole-release PAR2 read into one article fetch.
$14.95 1 month 20 connections; $8.95 3 months; $7.95 12 months billed $95.40 with 50 connections and US+EU; 6642 days
The same vendor's KB quotes $16.95 1 month, $8.95 exclusive and $7.95 12-month, and 'up to 20 SSL-encrypted connections' - a stale page
'UsenetServer does not impose restrictions on the number of articles accessed by users.'

record.notes: Potential failure points: retention, indexer staleness, or a connection ceiling. The vendor gives a number for none of them; the useful part of this page is the 423/430 split, which lets a user distinguish a missing group from a missing article. A vendor KB article says article access is unrestricted and uncapped; that is the only statement about volume on the site.

extras.strongest_signal: 430 (article absent) vs 423 (article number absent in a known group)
extras.account_states: article-level states only on the page read
